common_name: Silver Lace Brunnera (Lace-Veined Silver Heartleaf Bugloss)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Silver Lace will not come true from seed and must be propagated by division.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Silver Lace carries heart-shaped leaves overlaid with bright silver in a fine, lace-like network, leaving the green venation visible as delicate tracery rather than bold broad veins. Small sprays of sky-blue, forget-me-not-like flowers rise above the emerging foliage in early spring, and the cultivar is notable as the parent from which the heat-tolerant sport 'Sea Heart' arose.

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to full shade, with some tolerance of morning sun in cooler climates.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Alba is the plain-leaved, white-flowered form of Siberian bugloss, bearing the same rough-textured, heart-shaped green leaves as the species but with airy sprays of pure white blooms in early spring instead of the typical sky blue. Grown mainly by collectors assembling the full color range of brunnera flowers; divide congested clumps in spring or fall to maintain vigor.

common_name: Bowles' Red Lungwort (Early Coral-Red Flowered Lungwort)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Divide congested clumps every 3-4 years after flowering.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Bowles' Red is a long-cultivated selection of Pulmonaria rubra named for English plantsman E. A. Bowles, grown for velvety, plain to faintly spotted green leaves and unusually early, warm coral-red tubular flowers that open from late winter into early spring, often while frost still lingers. It is more vigorous and spreading than many named hybrids, forming a useful groundcover beneath deciduous shrubs.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes

common_name: Blauer Hugel Lungwort (Compact German Longleaf Lungwort)

planting.note: Plant divisions in early spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; keep soil evenly moist through the first season.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Blauer Hugel ('Blue Hill') is a German-bred selection of the narrow-leaved lungwort valued for compact, tidy clumps of slender, silver-spotted green leaves and vivid, saturated blue flowers held just above the foliage in early to mid-spring. Its small stature suits the front of a shaded border, rock-garden edges, or containers; divide crowded clumps every few years to maintain flowering vigor.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Fruhlingshimmel (German for 'spring sky') bears broad, heavily silver-spotted leaves typical of the saccharata group, with flower clusters that open white, pass through pink, and mature to blue, often showing all three colors at once in early to mid-spring. Cut back tattered summer foliage to refresh the clump and keep the silvering bright for the following spring.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Raspberry Ice is a patented lungwort with lance-shaped leaves edged in crisp white and overlaid with silvery, frosted mottling across a greyed-green blade. In spring it produces dense clusters of small flowers that open raspberry-red and deepen toward red-purple as they age, with many blooms open at once for a long early to mid-season display.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Irish Spring is a patented lungwort bred for strong resistance to powdery mildew, keeping its deep green, lime-variegated leaves clean through summer. Flowers open light rose-red in early spring and shift through blue-rose tones before maturing to deep violet-blue.
